q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Short answer: the data does show ROAS increased modestly while profit worsened versus the business’s usual days — Net ROAS rose to 0.87x (2026-10-09..2026-10-15) from 0.80x the prior week (+8.0%), but net profit for the same window was a loss of INR -42,274 and is worse than the usual recent days. In plain terms: efficiency per rupee of ad spend went up, but the business sold less and lost contribution margin, so the P&L weakened.

What’s behind it (largest impacts first)
- Contribution margin fell sharply: net contribution margin fell from INR 3,56,702 → INR 2,77,546 (2026-10-02..2026-10-08 → 2026-10-09..2026-10-15, −22.2%). This cut in margin is the main driver of the weaker net profit (it explains ~97% of the net-profit move in the period).
- Net sales dropped: P&L net sales dropped INR 6,16,090 → INR 4,50,676 (−26.8%), so there was less revenue base to cover fixed costs and the remaining ad spend.
- Ad spend fell (improved ROAS): ad spend (P&L basis) dropped INR 4,28,544 → INR 3,19,820 (−25.4%). Lower absolute spend raised ROAS (spend fell more than the margin-per-order did), but it did not prevent the profit decline because the sales drop removed the bulk of contribution margin.
- Mix / funnel effects and Simpson’s-paradox: contribution margin per order actually rose while ad-spend per order also rose; the net effect increased ROAS but volumes (orders, landing-page views, link clicks) fell sharply (orders 376 → 235, −37.5%), so overall profit fell.

Worth checking: dig into which channels/products lost the most contribution margin (meta advertising and its product mix were highlighted in the diagnosis) and whether the net sales decline is due to lower demand, fewer active campaigns, or a pricing/discount change.

Period: 2026-10-09..2026-10-15 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-16
